newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China sees US$281 billion trade turnover for 1996.
newsitem.headline: China sees US$281 billion trade turnover for 1996.

text.p: China's total trade in 1996 will reach a value of US$281 billion and exports will roughly equal imports, a spokesman for China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation (MOFTEC) said on Thursday.
"The value of exports has decreased a little bit in the first half of 1996, due to some problems," Hu Zhaoqing told a Hong Kong news conference.
He said the drop was normal given China's sharp export growth over the past two years.
"By the end of the second half, those problems will have been adjusted, and we will reach our trade target of US$281 billion." Exports and imports would be roughly balanced.
An earlier estimate from China's State Information Center saw China's 1996 trade surplus near US$4 billion. Exports were forecast at US$157 billion and imports at US$153 billion.

For the first time, MOFTEC held a press conference announcing the autumn session of China's Export Commodities Fair in Hong Kong, which is set to revert to China in 1997. He said Hong Kong was an important business partner for China.

Business transacted with Hong Kong and Macau at the last fair accounted for 19 percent (US$1.7 billion) of the total and it was visited by 21,239 business people from Hong Kong and Macau or 41 percent of the total, Hu said.
China's Export Commodities Fair, scheduled to open on October 15 in Guangzhou, is held twice a year and is expected this time to generate about US$10 billion of business.
The annual export volume of the fair accounts for about one-fifth of the country's total, Hu said.
